newsitem.title: UK: UK electricity stocks slip after Goldman downgrade.
newsitem.headline: UK electricity stocks slip after Goldman downgrade.

text.p: Shares in UK regional electricity companies (Recs) fell on Tuesday as Goldman Sachs lowered its ratings on a number of stocks after a review of the sector.

Assuming industry regulator Offer takes a similar approach in its 2000 industry price review as for National Grid recently, a valuation of the sector on a discounted cash flow and sum of the parts basis indicates dividend payouts will have to be cut, said Goldman analyst Philip Green.
The two companies faced with the largest dividend cuts would be Northern Electric and London Electric, he said.
Southern Electric and East Midlands Electricity come out as the top picks on a long term fundamental view relative to sector.
Green's analysis is based on the asumption that the current regulatory system is not changed fundamentally by a Labour government and his forecasts include a windfall levy of one billion stg.

Shares in Northern Electric fell 8p to 488-1/2p after being cut to "market performer" from "trading buy". Yorkshire Electricity was down 7p to 744p and London Electric 10-1/2p to 590-1/2p after similar downgrades.
East Midland Electricity and Southern Electric were both downgraded to "market outperformer" from "trading buy" and the shares fell 3-1/2p to 505p and 2-1/2p to 617-1/2p respectively.
"Two recs stand out as offering slightly better value - Southern Electric and East Midlands," said Green.

"Yorkshire while weak on its regulatory positioning has stronger non-core businesses with more potential upside in value than some of the others. Northern has a much higher financial risk profile and less resilience to regulatory change than the peer group."
Shares in the sector were weak yesterday after BZW also warned companies may find dividend policies unsustainable beyond 2000.
